title: "find.bubbles"
subtitle: "Detect bubbling (ebullition) events in a chamber incubation time series"
---

<h2>Description</h2>

<p>Identifies bubbling events in a gas concentration time series by analysing
rolling dispersion within a moving window. Dispersion can be quantified from
the rolling median absolute deviation (<code>"mad"</code>), the rolling variance
(<code>"variance"</code>), or the rolling MAD of the first differences
(<code>"diff"</code>). Contiguous periods where dispersion exceeds an adaptive
threshold are flagged as candidate bubbling events. For each event the size
of the concentration step is then estimated with a local step-dummy
regression that separates the abrupt bubble step from the underlying
diffusive trend.
</p>


<h2>Usage</h2>

<pre><code class='language-R'>find.bubbles(
  df,
  bubble_source,
  window.size = 15,
  dt = 1,
  method = c("mad", "variance", "diff"),
  var.quantile = 0.7,
  k = 4,
  min_ratio = 3,
  min_sd = NULL,
  min_gap = 10,
  min_length = 5,
  max_reg_window = 120,
  reg.min.obs = 10,
  min_magnitude = 5,
  min_snr = NULL
)
</code></pre>


<h2>Arguments</h2>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="df">df</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data.frame containing the incubation time series. Must include an
<code>Etime</code> column (elapsed time, seconds) and the concentration column
named by <code>bubble_source</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble_source">bubble_source</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character; name of the concentration column used for
detection (e.g. <code>"CH4dry_ppb"</code>).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="window.size">window.size</code></td>
<td>
<p>Integer; width of the moving window (in interpolated time
steps) used to compute rolling dispersion. Default <code>15</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="dt">dt</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; temporal resolution (seconds) of the regular grid the
signal is interpolated onto before rolling statistics. Default <code>1</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character; dispersion metric. One of <code>"mad"</code> (default),
<code>"variance"</code> or <code>"diff"</code>. <code>"diff"</code> applies the rolling MAD to
the first differences of the signal and is largely insensitive to a linear
diffusive trend, so it is recommended when diffusion is strong (see
Details).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="var.quantile">var.quantile</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric in (0, 1); empirical quantile of the rolling
dispersion distribution used in the adaptive threshold. Default <code>0.7</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="k">k</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; multiplier on the MAD of the rolling dispersion in the
robust threshold (<code class="reqn">median + k \times MAD</code>). Larger values are more
conservative. Default <code>4</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_ratio">min_ratio</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; minimum ratio of the maximum to the median rolling
dispersion required before any detection is attempted. Guards against
detections in flat, low-variance incubations. Default <code>3</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_sd">min_sd</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric or <code>NULL</code>; if set, incubations whose overall
standard deviation is below this value return <code>NULL</code> (no detection).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_gap">min_gap</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; events separated by less than this gap (seconds) are
merged. Default <code>10</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_length">min_length</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; minimum event duration (seconds) to retain.
Default <code>5</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="max_reg_window">max_reg_window</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; maximum half-window (seconds) used for the
local magnitude regression around each event. Default <code>120</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="reg.min.obs">reg.min.obs</code></td>
<td>
<p>Integer; minimum observations required for the magnitude
regression. Default <code>10</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_magnitude">min_magnitude</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric or <code>NULL</code>; minimum absolute step magnitude
(same units as <code>bubble_source</code>) to retain an event. Default <code>5</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="min_snr">min_snr</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric or <code>NULL</code>; if set, minimum signal-to-noise ratio
(<code>|magnitude| / SE</code>) to retain an event.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h2>Details</h2>

<p>The signal is first robustly standardised (median / MAD) and interpolated
onto a regular <code>dt</code>-second grid. Rolling dispersion is then computed and
compared to an adaptive threshold defined as the maximum of an empirical
quantile (<code>var.quantile</code>) and a robust bound (<code class="reqn">median + k \times
MAD</code>). Contiguous supra-threshold runs are merged (<code>min_gap</code>) and
filtered by duration (<code>min_length</code>).
</p>
<p>A steep but purely diffusive rise inflates the rolling variance/MAD even in
the absence of bubbles, which can produce false positives. The <code>"diff"</code>
method mitigates this by operating on the increments of the signal: a genuine
ebullition step produces a large positive spike in the first differences,
whereas a linear diffusive trend produces roughly constant increments and
therefore low differenced dispersion.
</p>
<p>Event magnitude is estimated with the local model
</p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">C_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t + \beta_2 I(t \ge t_b)</code>
</p>

<p>where <code class="reqn">I(t \ge t_b)</code> is a step dummy at the event start; <code class="reqn">\beta_2</code> is
the estimated magnitude. Only events with a positive magnitude are retained
(ebullition adds gas to the headspace).
</p>


<h2>Value</h2>

<p>A data.frame with one row per retained bubbling event and columns
<code>start</code>, <code>end</code>, <code>magnitude</code>, <code>SE</code>, <code>slope</code> and
<code>n_used</code>; or <code>NULL</code> if no events are detected or the series does
not meet the minimum variability criteria.
</p>


<h2>Examples</h2>

<pre><code class='language-R'>## Not run: 
bubbles &lt;- find.bubbles(df = incubation_data,
                        bubble_source = "CH4dry_ppb",
                        window.size = 15,
                        method = "diff")

## End(Not run)

</code></pre>
